messages:
claire (PM): Quick sync — ACME asked for a 'burst window SLA' for their Dedicated pilot: 99.95% availability for requests served from their reserved pool measured in 15m windows. They also want telemetry-driven autoscale hooks (p90/p95 queue depth triggers) and a QA acceptance checklist before cutover. Can we scope what we can commit to by EOW? cc @anne @raj

anne (Eng): Do we know whether they mean guaranteed RPS or guaranteed success rate? Those map to different work (capacity vs. graceful degradation).

raj (Infra): My read from their email: they care about observable failures (request errors / 5xx) during bursts. For autoscale hooks we can expose a webhook + prewarm API that operators can call. Roughly 2 sprints to make it production-ready unless we limit config surface.

olivia (SRE): Heads-up — promising 99.95% in 15m windows is risky without a fallback. If we fully commit we need an automatic spillover to hosted models + circuit breaker and a runbook for rapid rollback. Do we have those?

sam (Support): ACME also asked for request-level audit logs and retention for the pilot. We can provide traces and per-tenant telemetry, but retention/PII needs confirming.

claire (PM): Proposed scope for MVP (to present to ACME):
- Provide operator-configurable autoscale triggers + webhook-based prewarm (soft prewarm for pilot)
- Canary cutover with automatic fallback to hosted model variant on errors
- QA acceptance checklist + runbook for cutover

Can folks call out anything missing or suggest scope reductions?

anne (Eng): Canary + fallback is smart. If we make triggers operator-configurable (rather than product-exposed UI) we can shorten delivery. Estimated infra work: ~6 dev-weeks total (2w design + 4w impl + tests).

raj (Infra): Prototype config example (will put real YAML in ticket):
```
autoscale:
  trigger:
    metric: queue_depth_p95
    threshold: 120
    window: 60s
  action:
    prewarm: 2-gpus
    timeout: 300s
```
This gives us a deterministic hook we can wire into prewarm/autoscaler.

olivia (SRE): QA items I want in the checklist:
- Load test at 2x expected burst profile
- Chaos test: drop a region / simulate GPU failure and ensure fallback
- Canary traffic window with real requests and rollback criteria defined
- Metric alerts for queue depth, tail-latency and error-rate

claire (PM): Draft QA acceptance checklist for the pilot (for discussion with ACME):
- SLO mapping defined (15m window -> target 99.95% success)
- Autoscale trigger config documented + example YAML
- Canary plan with traffic ramp and explicit rollback thresholds
- Telemetry access provided to ACME (read-only dashboards) + retention stated
- Security checklist: KMS/HSM integration verified for any keys used
- Cutover runbook with support/onsite contacts and post-cutover monitoring plan

marco (Legal): We can't commit to an SLA number in public docs or without an amendment to the enterprise contract. Suggest we label it a 'pilot target' and keep contractual SLA language until legal signoff.

claire (PM): Good point — we'll present as 'pilot target' and let legal draft contract language.

deploy-bot: ticket PIOT-342 created by @claire for "ACME dedicated burst pilot: autoscale + QA"

anne (Eng): 👍 I'll add the rough estimates to the JIRA ticket today.

olivia (SRE): 👀 I'll start a test harness skeleton and share a benchmark plan by Wednesday.

sam (Support): I'll line up support coverage for cutover day and confirm logging requirements with ACME.

claire (PM): Thanks. Next steps: @anne estimate due EOD tomorrow, @raj prototype webhook + config mock by Thu, @olivia initial tests by Wed. I'll coordinate calendar with ACME and follow up with legal. Reconvene Fri 11am if any blockers.
